items.text: Every distinct planted blocker survives aggregation: B1 fixed-30-day proration (billing.js), B2 teamName interpolated into SQL (teams.js findMembers), B3 non-atomic member+team delete (teams.js removeTeam), B4 discount/tax order disagreement between checkoutTotal and renewalTotal (billing.js), B5 seat check-then-act race (teams.js addMember), B6 naive trial date parse (notify.js), B7 null-owner crash (notify.js). None is dropped by axis budgeting or the finding cap.
The exact-duplicate pair (B7: the same null-owner crash reachable from invoiceEmail and renewalNotice — same root, same consequence, same fix) is merged into ONE finding, not listed twice.

The shared-root pair (B6 naive date parse) keeps BOTH consequences explicit — the expiry decision (trialExpired) and the displayed date (trialBanner) — whether as two findings or one finding naming both; merging them into a single-consequence mention fails.

The non-blocker noise budget cannot hide a blocker: all 7 blockers are present even though the cap forces lower-severity findings (SF1 missing teams tests, SF2 swallowed gateway error, N1 magic literal) to compete for space.
Final finding order is deterministic after deduplication (severity-first, stable within severity), and at least one of SF1/SF2 survives as a should-fix.
